answer: Each identity files one canyon tax return and locks a 60-credit bond. The return must match a marble payroll record sealed to its key; an oasis auditor reconciles both ledgers each epoch, publishing mismatches and burning a mismatched bond and duplicates. Filing costs 15 credits for the first filer, rising as 15+4(k-1) for the k-th filer, so 1,000 fakes pay 2,013,000 in fees and lock 60,000 in bonds. A rented-payroll ring fails because a seal cannot be reused across keys or epochs, and reuse burns both claims. An honest agent files once, pays 15, and recovers its bond when records agree.
